story: At 7:17 on a humid, hazy Wednesday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is bench-testing a light strip controller and speaker amp in his garage, keeping the volume off since nothing is mounted yet. Across the way, Donna is hunting her club calendar for an open court slot so she can pencil in doubles practice with Gary. Hal sits content at his kitchen table, marking the golf cart and flamingo entries in his violation notebook as resolved and compliant. Meanwhile, Rosa is focused in her kitchen, checking her marinade and prepping what she can make ahead for Saturday's dinner.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-test the light strip controller and speaker amp, speaker volume off, nothing mounted yet
Donna (donna club calendar): Look for an open court slot to pencil in doubles practice with Gary
Hal (hal violation notebook): Mark the cart and flamingo entries as resolved and compliant
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Check the marinade and prep what can be made ahead for Saturday's dinner

gary.thought_process: It's 7:17 AM, I'm home with the cart and workbench right here. My memory says I told myself no sound until tomorrow, and L-01 says exterior mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, so I shouldn't hang more on the outside until the paperwork is squared away. Still, I can work on the stuff that isn't touching the street-facing side: bench-test the speaker amp and the light strip controller on the workbench so it's ready to go once approved. That keeps me busy and useful without breaking a rule, and it's quiet enough since the sound stays off until tomorrow anyway. Then I'll head out to Rosa's dinner prep and the practice with Hal and Donna on time.

parameters.content: Bench-test the light strip controller and speaker amp, speaker volume off, nothing mounted yet

donna.thought_process: It's a quiet morning at home and nobody is nearby. Gary and I are already on the doubles ladder as Pruitt-Kowalski, and he headed out to meet Hal. I should keep the momentum going, so I'll check my club calendar to find open court time for our next practice and slot it in without running afoul of the two-hour reservation limit.

parameters.content: Look for an open court slot to pencil in doubles practice with Gary

hal.thought_process: Tick 131 had me heading to Rosa's House, but the engine says I'm at Hal's House at 7:17 AM Wednesday, so a new morning has started and the dinner is Saturday at six. Nobody is within sight. My old goal of reporting Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos is moot: Gary kept his word and Donna trimmed down to three. The honest, by-the-book thing is to log the closed matters in my violation notebook so the record is accurate and the complaint is retired.

parameters.content: Mark the cart and flamingo entries as resolved and compliant

rosa.thought_process: It's 7:17 AM Wednesday and I'm alone in the kitchen. The marinade is started and the grocery list is finalized from the last few ticks. Gary, Donna, and Hal are all invited for Saturday at six, and nobody is nearby, so there's no one to speak to and nothing to repeat. The useful next step is the marinade and the prep I set aside, so I'll check on it and organize what can be made ahead. Then I can head out for groceries.

parameters.content: Check the marinade and prep what can be made ahead for Saturday's dinner

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
